answer: Memory-hard residency proofs. Each seat must keep a private 2 GB table, built from its own key with a memory-hard hash and split into 64 MB walnut blocks. Every epoch the verifier takes a zephyr seed from the beacon, derives 8 random block indices and wants those entries back within 2 seconds, which only works if the table sits in RAM. A seat whose latency ranks at the nadir of the field loses its vote weight. So 500 fakes need 1 TB of live RAM every epoch, caught or not.
